children: Romania's consolidated budget deficit was 2.34% of economic output at end-July, the finance ministry said on Monday, sharply down from a shortfall of 3.99% posted in the same period of 2025.
Romania, whose coalition government collapsed in early May without being replaced yet, is targeting a deficit of 6.2% of output this year and analysts said it was on track to meet that goal.

However, it must continue lowering the deficit gradually to the European Union's threshold of 3% of economic output, and its ability to do so is key to Romania keeping its sovereign rating on the last rung of investment grade.
Data released on Monday showed the deficit stood at 48.08 billion lei ($10.60 billion). Revenue for the first seven months amounted to 412.3 billion lei, or 20.1% of output.
The budget for this year is underpinned by EU recovery and resilience funds and based on an economic growth assumption of 1%.
Meanwhile, the economy continued to contract in the second quarter, with the outlook further clouded by political instability and a drought-induced energy crisis.

The four parliamentary parties that used to form the now defunct coalition government failed to agree on the draft of a single wage bill for the public sector that was a key requirement for EU recovery funds.

The bill, which was supposed to make public sector wage spending more predictable and reduce imbalances, was attached to some €770 million worth of EU recovery funds the country is now poised to lose.
Analysts said the bill's failure undermined Romania's credibility abroad on enforcing reforms and cutting its deficit.
